2	
3	Source anchor: signed/pushed `244c935f9e715236e9f2c2783f3bb6bee24706e1`.
4	
5	## Demonstrated seam
6	
7	The remaining failure is not another scan-custody or projection defect.
8	`creator-close.ts::issuanceRetirementCandidate()` derives and signs exactly one
9	frontier for `registration.issuanceScope`, which is the close owner's local
10	author. `creator-transition-advance.ts::openVerifiedCreatorHistoricalIssuance()`
11	requires exactly one retirement candidate. `v3-live.ts` can carry that
12	capability through recovery for a foreign local scope after 0c1e, but
13	`authenticatedCoveredHistoricalOutboxRow()` deliberately requires both
14	`scopeAuthorMatches` and `identity.author === issuanceScope.author`. A
15	non-creator writer's old row therefore has no authenticated cumulative frontier
16	once it is older than both current and displaced epoch authority.
17	
18	The close owner cannot safely reuse the writer's durable issuance store. The
19	`DurableIssuanceStore` is injected for one local `(objectId, author)` scope;
20	successor reopen explicitly permits nonzero lineage only for the reopening
21	author and requires every other current writer's lineage in that local store to
22	be zero. The close owner does, however, hold the authenticated bounded current
23	epoch graph and both current and staged-successor ACL snapshots. That graph can
24	prove an admitted dense per-author prefix, but the current one-author record
25	cannot encode it.
26	
27	## Candidate decision
28	
29	| Candidate | Authentication | Epoch growth | Compatibility / disposition |
30	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
31	| Treat any creator carrier as authority for every writer | None for the selected writer frontier | Constant | Rejected: suppresses arbitrary foreign rows under a creator-only number. |
32	| Have each writer self-sign its retirement frontier | Proves issuance, not admission into the certified close | Constant per writer | Rejected without creator/QC countersignature; changes authority and requires online writers at close. |
33	| Authenticate each old vertex with an RFC 9162 history inclusion/consistency proof | Strong when the exact leaf/index and current history root are bound | `O(log history)` proof and a proof-producing retained history/index | Rejected for this Phase-6 active-control seam: current production has no proof carrier/store, and ordinary reopen would depend on an age-growing proof/index owned by Phase 7. |
34	| Keep one signed record/candidate per writer ever seen | Direct stable-creator authentication | `O(lifetime writers)` and potentially `O(epoch)` under churn | Rejected: hides unbounded control growth in the AHE closure. |
35	| One creator-signed sorted frontier vector for the authenticated successor writer set | Stable creator signature plus adjacent current/successor trust, cut/QC, snapshot, ACL, and graph-derived dense prefixes | At most 64 entries per active record and two rollback generations | Selected implementation family, subject to the compatibility boundary below. It requires a new versioned protocol control carrier and therefore cannot be implemented inside 0c1f without a separately reviewed high-risk prerequisite. |
36	| Sparse authenticated dictionary / recursive accumulator | Can cover unbounded historical author churn with a constant root | Root is constant, but witnesses/node/proving state and availability move elsewhere | Rejected for now: either ordinary reopen depends on an unbounded proof store or the design introduces new accumulator/SNARK dependencies and setup. It may be reconsidered only if the bounded current-writer vector cannot satisfy reviewed lifecycle semantics. |
37	
38	## Selected proof obligations
39	
40	The proposed aggregate record is a new creator-signed, versioned, non-root
41	control carrier. It binds object and genesis identity; current and successor
42	epoch/anchor; current and successor ACL digests; cut digest; commit-QC ref;
43	snapshot-manifest digest; one prior aggregate digest or a genesis sentinel; and
44	an author-sorted vector of exact successor-writer entries. Each entry is
45	`{author, admittedAuthorSequence}`, where the boundary may be null for a writer
46	with no certified issuance. The vector is exact for the authenticated successor
47	ACL's writer set, has no duplicate, omitted, extra, or reordered author, and is
48	bounded by the existing latched-ACL maximum of 64 members.
49	
50	For a continuing writer, the new boundary starts at the previously opened
51	entry and advances only across the exact contiguous author-sequence prefix in
52	the authenticated current close graph. For a newly authorized writer it starts
53	at null and can advance only from sequence zero. Gaps, duplicates, conflicting
54	same-slot digests, a sequence regression, a graph/ACL author mismatch, or a
55	frontier above the proven dense prefix cannot advance that entry. A row above a
56	nonadvanced boundary remains visible/pending and cannot be hidden as
57	historical. The stable creator signer attests admission, not merely issuance;
58	the retained local-issued/outbox exact-byte comparison and non-equivocating
59	local issuer assumption remain unchanged.
60	
61	Cold recovery opens the aggregate only against the independently authenticated
62	current floor and adjacent cut/QC/snapshot/ACL facts, selects exactly the local
63	issuance author entry, and gives the private historical classifier that one
64	boundary. It does not expose the entire vector as public authority. Published
65	and pending historical rows retain their current distinct behavior; pending
66	rows are reissued/completed before the original is marked, while no row beyond
67	the authenticated entry is suppressed. The three filter classes share one
68	logical-scan counter and one `maxEpochVertices` ceiling.
69	
70	## Compatibility boundary and stop condition
71	
72	The existing `drp-creator-issuance-retirement-state` v1 record is immutable
73	shipped evidence and contains only one author. An additive aggregate carrier
74	can coexist during migration, but an old room with prior non-creator issuance
75	cannot synthesize that writer's historical frontier from the current epoch
76	alone. It must either retain/retrieve independently authenticated history or
77	fail with an explicit compatibility error. No migration may infer a frontier
78	from untrusted local lineage.
79	
80	ACL removal can drop an author from the next active vector because that author
81	cannot reopen under the successor ACL and the retained rollback generation
82	still holds the prior vector. Re-adding the same key after its frontier has
83	left the rollback window is unresolved: the current `(objectId, author)`
84	issuance scope has no membership-incarnation field, and accepting its nonzero
85	lineage as a new writer would be unsafe. The implementation prerequisite must
86	either define an authenticated compact re-entry proof or explicitly reject
87	same-key re-add with nonzero lineage and assign the broader migration before a
88	golden path relies on it. It may not retain every removed author forever.
89	
90	Because the selected family adds a signed carrier kind/fields, protocol
91	prepare/open/resolve behavior, control-closure transition law, compatibility
92	path, and browser-visible persisted bytes, this audit stops before production
93	editing. D.110c-0c1f1 must receive a high-risk Grok/Kimi/Opus plan review. It
94	must not change the trust root, creator-only authority, thresholds,
95	dependencies, public room API, workload, or memory/resource ceilings while
96	implementing the carrier.
